system.name: Scalio
system.one_liner: a DPU-based JBOF key-value store that offloads NVMe-oF target processing to scale storage throughput

content.subject: how a cache slot's occupied/complete flags step through four states under Fill, Lock, Invalidate, and Evict

elements.name: Legends
elements.role: header row naming the four fields shown in every state's record: key, occupied, value, complete

elements.name: occupied
elements.role: flag indicating whether the slot holds a valid key

elements.name: value
elements.role: field holding the slot's value data

elements.name: complete
elements.role: flag indicating whether the value has been fully written

elements.name: (A) A clean empty slot
elements.role: occupied=0, complete=1: the slot holds no valid data and is safe to reuse

elements.name: (D) Invalidated while value being filled
elements.role: occupied=0, complete=0, value partially written: the slot was invalidated before its in-flight fill finished

elements.name: (C) A valid cache item
elements.role: occupied=1, complete=1: the slot holds a fully written, valid key/value pair

elements.name: (B) Value being filled
elements.role: occupied=1, complete=0, value partially written: the slot is claimed and its value is still being written

relations.what: locking a clean slot claims it and starts writing a new value
the fill completes while the slot is still claimed, producing a fully written valid item
the slot is invalidated (unclaimed) before its in-flight fill finishes
the stale fill completes on an already-invalidated slot, leaving it clean and reusable
the valid item is invalidated or evicted, returning the slot to a clean, reusable state
invalidating an already-clean slot has no further effect
invalidating an already-invalidated slot has no further effect

content.key_idea: Two per-slot flags, occupied and complete, define four states - clean, being filled, valid, and invalidated-while-filling - and the Fill/Lock/Invalidate/Evict transitions between them let Scalio detect the race where a slot is invalidated while still being filled.
content.reading_order: Top-left (A) reads right to (D) via Fill; bottom-left (C) reads right to (B) via Fill, with vertical and diagonal arrows linking the two rows and looping self-invalidations.

palette.used_for: all state boxes, record cells, arrows, and text - the figure is a monochrome black-and-white line diagram with no colour coding

style.stroke: uniform thin black strokes (median ~1.15pt), solid, no dashing
style.arrows: thin black straight and curved arrows (6 heads, 2 curved) labelled with the transition name

encoding.color_means: no colour is used; the figure is monochrome black-and-white
encoding.line_style_means: all edges are solid lines; two are curved self-loops and the rest are straight arrows between states
encoding.state_means: each of the four states is drawn as its own labelled record box (A/B/C/D) with the occupied and complete flag values shown as 0/1 inside the cells, so the flag bits themselves distinguish the states
encoding.marker_means: the letters (A)-(D) name each state; 0/1 values inside the record cells show the occupied and complete flag settings for that state
encoding.emphasis: the record layout is repeated identically in every state so only the flag values and the value/key cell contents change between states
reusable_patterns: a 4-state machine drawn as four repeated record-layout boxes in a 2x2 grid, connected by labelled transition arrows including two self-loops
weaknesses: the arrow from (D) to (A) and from (B) to (C) share the same 'Fill' label, so the two different completions are only distinguishable by which state they originate from
the figure does not show which entity (client, background thread) triggers each transition

evidence: The core of this protocol is based on two flags — occupied and complete
These two flags result in four distinct states
A slot is empty and safe to be reused when occupied is false and complete is true.

summary: Figure 9 defines the four-state lifecycle of a Scalio cache slot, driven by two flags recorded in each slot's record - occupied (does the slot hold a valid key) and complete (has the value been fully written). State (A), a clean empty slot, has occupied=0 and complete=1 and is safe to reuse; a Lock transition claims it and moves it to (B), value being filled (occupied=1, complete=0). From (B), a Fill completing normally reaches (C), a valid cache item (occupied=1, complete=1), while an Invalidate during the fill instead reaches (D), invalidated while value being filled (occupied=0, complete=0). A stale Fill completing from (D) simply resets the slot back to (A), and Invalidate/Evict on (C) also returns it to (A); invalidating an already-clean (A) or already-invalidated (D) slot is a no-op self-loop.
summary_zh: 图9定义Scalio缓存槽四态生命周期，由occupied/complete标志决定：(A)空槽经Lock到(B)填充中；(B)完成经Fill到(C)有效项，中途Invalidate则到(D)；(D)/(C)最终都回到(A)。
